Buscamos personas que no solo sean competentes, sino que tengan la actitud correcta.

La experiencia y las cualificaciones importan, pero la mentalidad importa más. Creemos que una ética de trabajo sólida, la voluntad de mejorar y la capacidad de tomar responsabilidad son los factores que determinan el éxito a largo plazo.

Con la mentalidad adecuada, puedes aprender rápido, crecer en el rol y generar impacto real, incluso si no tienes todas las respuestas desde el primer día.

Valoramos a las personas que asumen responsabilidades, superan los desafíos y siguen subiendo el nivel. Personas que aportan energía al equipo, desafían a los demás y nos ayudan a avanzar juntos.

About FlexGen

Based in Durham, N.C., FlexGen is an innovative software and services provider in the global energy storage sector. At the forefront of the energy transition, FlexGen leverages decades of engineering and software expertise to help shape the future of sustainable power both in the United States and globally. FlexGen's HybridOS™ software seamlessly integrates with any hardware vendor and with both traditional and renewable power sources. Our advanced analytics and AI-driven insights enable energy storage owners to effectively deploy diverse power market strategies and integrate various generation forms, enhancing grid stability and increasing economic returns. With 1.5M hours of runtime and 8 GWh of energy storage systems managed with HybridOS™, FlexGen provides field-tested software and services solutions that are trusted by the most technically and commercially demanding developers, utilities, government agencies, and industrial companies in the world.

Position Description:

The Procurement Manager will lead and oversee the procurement activities for major energy storage projects worldwide. You will manage project teams throughout all stages to ensure their supply needs are met promptly and efficiently. Effective day-to-day communication with internal team members and suppliers is essential to guide the purchasing requests through various phases necessary to deliver successful purchase orders. This role requires the ability to manage several projects in different life cycles simultaneously within a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

The Procurement Manager will be responsible for managing and optimizing the procurement of materials, components, and services for Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) projects. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented approach to sourcing and purchasing, combined with deep knowledge of the energy storage sector, its supply chain dynamics, and the technical aspects of BESS components. The Procurement Manager will play a pivotal role in negotiating favorable terms, driving cost efficiency, quality control, and timely delivery of goods while ensuring alignment with company objectives and compliance with industry regulations.

  • Procurement and Strategy Planning:

    • Identify key suppliers and vendors, fostering long-term relationships while maintaining competitive pricing and reliability
    • Conduct market research and analysis to identify new sourcing opportunities and mitigate risks in the supply chain
    • Monitor industry trends, emerging technologies, and market conditions affecting pricing, availability, and product specifications in the BESS market
  • Vendor Management & Supplier Relations
    • Manage the vendor selection process, including conducting supplier audits, negotiating contracts, and ensuring compliance with specifications, quality standards, and delivery schedules
    • Maintain effective communication with suppliers, addressing any performance issues or supply chain disruptions promptly
    • Build and maintain strong partnerships with key suppliers, collaborating on product improvements and cost-reduction initiatives

    • Ensure compliance with industry standards, legal requirements, and company policies related to procurement, quality control, health and safety, and sustainability

  • Strong knowledge of procurement processes, contract negotiation, and supplier relationship management

Self-directed individuals who take full ownership of pipeline and operate with a sense of urgency from day one

Team players who collaborate cross-functionally and elevate those around them

High-standards professionals who treat enterprise sales as a craft

You run the operational engine of a small portfolio of venture funds. You are in the GP's WhatsApp group. You are the named person behind their back-office inbox. When their LP is stuck in KYC, when a founder sends over a convertible note to sign "today, ideally," when a fund-of-funds sends a seven-question due-diligence list covering fee mechanics and cross-border tax treatment, you handle it, end to end.

The work is fund operations: onboarding, closings, capital calls, deal execution, reporting, and everything in between. But almost every one of those operations runs through legal documents, LPAs, subscription agreements, CLAs, side letters, which is why we require legal training. Not to give legal advice (we have internal legal and external counsel for that), but because an operator who can't read the documents is blocked twenty times a day, and one who can is unstoppable.

This is not a support queue, and it is not a law firm associate track. You own outcomes for named clients whose fundraises and deals move at startup speed, alongside an engineering team that ships fixes to the things you flag, often the same day.

Elsewhere in the industry, this job doesn't exist as one job. The large US platforms split it into four or five: a relations associate who talks to the GP, a deal-operations associate who executes, a fund accountant who closes the books, an in-house lawyer who reads the documents, an LP-relations team who answers investors. Every handoff between them is somewhere a client waits. We collapse the whole chain into one accountable person per client, and the only reason that works is the AI-first backend underneath you. At the incumbents, the people are the system. Here, the platform is the system: it reads the documents, drafts the answers, runs the checks, and moves the money at lightning speed, and you are its judgment, its signature, and its face to the client. One person with this backend outruns a five-person chain without it. That is the job.

Tasks

What you'll actually do:

A representative week, drawn from real client work:

  • Walk a GP's new LP through subscription and KYC, diagnose why their video identification keeps failing with our provider, and get them across the line with a fifteen-minute call.

  • Answer an institutional LP's due-diligence questionnaire: management fee mechanics, carry catch-up provisions, whether a foreign investor in an Austrian GmbH & Co KG has local tax filing obligations. Turn the best answers into reusable one-pagers so the next fund never has to wait.
  • Flag a side letter demanded by an LP as inappropriate for the check size, and give the GP language to decline without burning the relationship.

  • Feed everything you learn back into the platform. When you flag that founders don't know what a UBO is, the flow gets rewritten. When an onboarding step confuses LPs, engineering ships a fix. You are the platform's eyes in the field.

Requirements

  • An operator, first. You have founded, joined early, or run something. You default to unblocking rather than gold-plating, you know when "N/A" is a complete answer on a checklist, and you understand that a fund's LPs compare us to the best software products they use, not to other administrators.

  • Precision under speed. Wrong numbers in a capital call, a mismatched signature block, a missed clause in a document, these are not typos in this job, they are incidents. You are fast and exact, and you know which of the two to sacrifice when you must (never the second).
  • AI-fluent. You already work with LLMs daily, and "could the machine do this?" is your first question, not an afterthought. The role only works for people who treat the backend as a teammate to direct, not a tool to tolerate.
  • Fluent written and spoken English. German is a meaningful plus; so is any experience with EU or US fund structures.
  • Location and hours. Fully remote from Eastern Europe, South America, or the Philippines, with substantial daily overlap with Central European business hours.

Benefits

What you get:

  • A front-row seat to how venture funds actually work, formation to first close to deal execution to reporting, compressed into months instead of the decade it takes at a law firm or a legacy administrator.
  • AI leverage as the default, not the exception. The backend drafts, extracts, reconciles, and flags; you review, decide, and talk to humans. We automate the repetitive 80% so your time goes to judgment, clients, and edge cases, you will be more leveraged here than anywhere else you have worked, and you help decide what gets automated next.
  • Direct influence on the product. Your field observations become shipped features, sometimes within hours.
  • Direct access to founders, GPs, and LPs, the people most careers only ever see through six layers of hierarchy.
  • Compensation benchmarked at the top of your regional market, paid as a full-time remote engagement.

The test

If you read the week above and thought "that's five different jobs," this isn't for you. If you thought "finally, one job where I get to do all five", we should talk.

To apply, send us a short note (no cover letter theater) telling us about one deal, negotiation, or operational mess you personally untangled, and what you would have automated about it.

Position Summary The Asset Management & Reliability Manager provides national-level leadership in the design, implementation, and oversight of asset management and reliability programs across a portfolio of facilities. This role ensures that condition and criticality assessments, CMMS governance, and structured improvement programs such as Root Cause Analysis (RCA) are consistently applied. The Manager balances technical knowledge with leadership, strategy, and communication—ensuring asset management practices deliver compliance, lifecycle value, and operational reliability. Travel of approximately 50-75% is required to provide oversight, training, and alignment across the portfolio. Key Responsibilities Leadership & Oversight

  • Provide strategic leadership to establish and maintain reliability-focused asset management practices across all managed facilities.
  • Mentor and coach employees at various levels on CMMS use, asset assessment methods, and reliability improvement practices.
  • Build a culture of accountability, data-driven decision-making, and continuous improvement.
  • Represent the Asset Management & Reliability function in corporate, client, and executive forums, ensuring alignment between reliability programs and business objectives.

Asset Management & Assessments

  • Direct and execute standardized condition assessments portfolio-wide on mechanical, electrical, structural, and process assets, using standardized rating scales.
  • Document deterioration patterns, safety hazards, and compliance risks that affect lifecycle planning.
  • Apply RCM thinking during inspections, identifying potential functional failures and recommending optimized maintenance strategies.
  • Ensure data quality by validating asset tag numbers, hierarchy accuracy, and completeness in the CMMS.
  • Lead criticality assessments to assign business risk rankings and prioritize assets for investment, maintenance, and monitoring.
  • Analyze asset history and performance data to identify lifecycle risks and opportunities.
  • Translate assessment findings into portfolio-wide strategies that support capital planning, optimization, and asset replacement.

Reliability Improvement & RCA

  • Lead structured RCA investigations for asset failures, compliance incidents, safety events, or recurring operational issues.
  • Facilitate cross-site workshops to identify systemic causes and align corrective/preventive actions.
  • Ensure all RCA outcomes and improvement measures are captured, tracked, and verified in the CMMS.
  • Deliver trend reports that communicate lessons learned, systemic risks, and improvement initiatives to leadership and clients.
  • Champion continuous improvement by embedding reliability-based practices into daily facility operations.

CMMS Governance & Optimization

  • Standardize asset hierarchies, PM libraries, and coding structures to support portfolio-wide reporting.
  • Ability to train and certify users at multiple levels to ensure high-quality, accurate CMMS data entry.
  • Verify that assessment outcomes, RCA findings, and action items are consistently uploaded into CMMS, establishing a single source of truth for decision-making.

Reporting & Strategic Communication

  • Prepare professional, data-rich reports for leadership and clients on asset conditions, risk profiles, and portfolio reliability.
  • Translate technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations that inform business decisions.
  • Lead portfolio-level review sessions to align reliability objectives with operations, capital planning, and client expectations.
  • Provide executive-level reporting that demonstrates how asset management programs reduce risk, optimize cost, and extend asset lifecycle.

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Support

  • Coordinate reliability and asset management initiatives across facilities, ensuring consistent application of corporate standards.
  • Partner with facility managers, operations, engineering, and project management to embed reliability strategies into day-to-day operations.
  • Serve as the central liaison between site-level staff and corporate leadership, ensuring lessons learned are shared portfolio-wide.
  • Support procurement and investment decisions by providing lifecycle cost and risk-based input on asset selection.
  • Consolidate site-level activities into the CMMS, ensuring portfolio transparency and alignment.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Asset Management, Reliability, or related discipline (preferred).
  • Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in asset management, maintenance, or portfolio reliability management.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience across multi-site or national operations.
  • Strong expertise in asset criticality, RCA, and RCM methodologies.
  • Advanced knowledge of enterprise-level CMMS systems, including governance and reporting.
  • Proven skills in technical reporting, data analysis, and executive-level presentations.
  • Excellent training, facilitation, and mentoring skills.

Preferred certifications:

o CMRP (Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional) o CRL (Certified Reliability Leader) o IAM Certificate/Diploma in Asset Management

  • Willingness to travel 50-75% nationally.

Desired Skills

  • Familiarity with ISO 55000 asset management frameworks.
  • Experience in utilities, water/wastewater, or other regulated industrial environments.
  • Collaboration: Works effectively with facility teams and corporate leadership, serving as a trusted field advisor.
  • Professional Communication: Crafts reports and presentations that bridge technical detail and business relevance.
  • Adaptability: Thrives in varied environments, from industrial plants to utility sites, maintaining professionalism under pressure.

  • Proficiency in analytics/reporting platforms (e.g., Power BI, advanced Excel).
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills for RCA workshops, leadership sessions, and staff training.
  • Proven ability to link portfolio-wide asset management goals with tactical execution.

Position Details

College Board - Technology

Type: This is a full-time position

About the Team 

The Create team is committed to building and driving innovation for internal-facing web applications that support College Board’s core products. Our team consists of 2 small squads, each of which owns a unique, data-intensive, high-impact, single-page web application that represents our internal content creation processes. We own the full stack, from the infrastructure in AWS to the front-end and back-end code deployed there. We build everything serverless, in the cloud, leveraging current technologies and novel techniques to be a force-multiplier for the programs we serve. We are remote, but close-knit. We are strong advocates of work/life balance and flexibility with schedules when needed. We often accomplish our work through paired or mob programming. We are proactive, passionate, and outcome-oriented, putting a premium on quality and efficiency. We use Agile scrum to manage our work and deliver value regularly following a DevOps model. The impact of our efforts as creative problem-solvers and idea-generators leads to innovations and dramatic improvements in College Board’s biggest program applications, serving millions of students to help them take ownership of their future.

 

About the Opportunity  

As a Senior Full Stack Engineer on our Create team, you are a poly skilled technologist and problem-solver. You possess extensive knowledge and expertise designing, implementing, and testing performant and fault-tolerant serverless and container-based apps executing in the cloud. You are communicative, approachable, self-driven and energized by collaboration with teammates and a desire to stay abreast of new technologies. These traits along with your ability to learn quickly enable you to work harmoniously as you apply innovative, cloud-based solutions within College Board’s Technology group.

  

In this role, you will: 

  • Design, develop, and maintain user-facing features and back-end services using React, TypeScript, and AWS services, ensuring scalability and reliability
  • Design, implement, and maintain infrastructure as code (IaC) using AWS CDK
  • Work closely with cross-functional teams, provide technical guidance to junior developers, and drive the adoption of best practices and new technologies
  • Optimize application performance, implement automated testing using Playwright, and ensure technical feasibility and code quality through reviews
  • Solve complex problems using divergent thinking resulting in innovative solutions
  • Follow DevOps best practices including continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) practice of rapidly implementing, testing, and delivering high-quality code
  • Develop and maintain a thorough understanding of our customer’s business processes and operations
  • Support team-centered, Agile software development

About you, you have:

  • Ideally 7+ years' experience in full stack development, building, testing, and managing web-based applications
  • At least 3 years of recent, strong, hands-on experience with React, TypeScript, Node.js and AWS
  • Experience working within the AWS cloud ecosystem, including serverless architecture and resources such as Lambda, Gateway API, SNS, SQS, S3, Step Functions, IAM, CloudWatch, CloudTrail, and DynamoDB
  • A passion for learning, driving change, and proposing solutions to complex problems
  • Bachelor’s and/or master’s degree in computer science, systems engineering, information systems or similar

All roles at College Board require:

  • A passion for expanding educational and career opportunities and mission-driven work
  • Curiosity and enthusiasm for emerging technologies, with a willingness to experiment with and adopt new AI-driven solutions and a comfort learning and applying new digital tools independently and proactively. 
  • Clear and concise communication skills, written and verbal
  • A learner's mindset and a commitment to growth: welcoming diverse perspectives, giving and receiving timely, respectful feedback, and continuously improving through iterative learning and user input.
  • A drive for impact and excellence: solving complex problems, making data-informed decisions, prioritizing what matters most, and continuously improving through learning, user input, and external benchmarking.
  • A collaborative and empathetic approach: working across differences, fostering trust, and contributing to a culture of shared success.
  • Travel: The ability to travel 3-5 times a year to College Board offices or on behalf of College Board business
  • Work Authorization: Authorization to work in the United States for any employer without sponsorship

About Our Process 

  • Application review will begin immediately and will continue until the position is filled. This role is expected to accept applications for a minimum of 5 business days.
  • While the hiring process may vary, it generally includes: resume and application submission, recruiter phone/video screen, hiring manager interview, performance exercise such as live coding, a panel interview, a conversation with leadership and reference checks.

What We Offer

At College Board, we offer more than just a paycheck—we provide a meaningful career, a supportive team, and a comprehensive package designed to help you thrive. We’re a self-sustaining nonprofit that believes in fair and competitive compensation, grounded in your qualifications, experience, impact, and the market.

A Thoughtful Approach to Compensation

About the team

Zillow operates at the intersection of one of the most consequential industries in people's lives — and that visibility comes with complexity. This Manager of Corporate Communications will own a critical and specialized function within Zillow's Communications team: developing and executing communications strategy across litigation and regulatory matters.

This is a high-trust, high-autonomy role. You'll work directly with Legal, Executive Leadership and senior Comms partners to shape how Zillow responds to — and, where possible, gets ahead of — the media narratives that emerge from legal proceedings. You'll be the connective tissue between our legal strategy and our public voice, ensuring those two things are never out of sync.

You won't have direct reports, but you will lead. You'll drive cross-functional workstreams, bring clarity to ambiguous situations, and be the recognized owner of litigation communications at Zillow.

About the role

Own the litigation communications function end-to-end.

You'll develop proactive and reactive communications strategies for litigation, regulatory, and legal risk matters — anticipating how cases may evolve in the press, preparing leadership for likely lines of questioning, and ensuring Zillow speaks with consistency and confidence. Your work product is polished and precise and you exercise strong, sound judgement, ability to assess and carry strategy through to execution and independently develop work that is ready for senior executive review.

Serve as a trusted strategic partner to Legal and the C-suite.

You'll operate in rooms with General Counsel, outside counsel and C-suite executives and will need the ability to influence decision-making and escalate needs to leadership with speed and clarity. You'll translate complex legal situations into clear communication positions, proactively flag communication risks, and regularly present solutions alongside the problems you identify.

Drive cross-functional projects with rigor and clarity.

You'll lead workstreams across Legal, Communications, Policy, and Investor Relations — defining objectives, building workback plans, and establishing RACI frameworks that keep complex, fast-moving matters organized. You anticipate the questions your stakeholders haven't thought to ask yet and show up with answers.

Manage media relationships in a specialized, high-stakes context.

You'll build and maintain relationships with journalists who cover legal, regulatory, and real estate industry beats — proactively shaping narratives where possible and responding with speed and precision when inquiries arrive. You understand how to work within legal constraints while still being an effective, credible media partner.

Monitor, adapt, and apply.

You'll track legal, regulatory and media developments that could affect Zillow, bring relevant intelligence back to the team and quickly integrate lessons into how you work.

Represent Comms in cross-functional forums.

You'll carry the broader Communications team's perspective into legal strategy discussions, stakeholder planning meetings, and executive briefings — advocating for communications interests and helping other functions understand what's at stake from a public narrative standpoint.

This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $109,000.00 - $174,000.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $103,500.00 - $165,300.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

  • You have deep experience in media relations and have spent meaningful time managing sensitive, high-stakes communications — whether in litigation, crisis, financial, or regulatory contexts.

  • You are an exceptional writer and verbal communicator.

  • Your presence in rooms with senior leadership is confident and credible.

  • You operate well with ambiguity and competing priorities. You don't wait to be told what to do; you identify what needs to happen and move toward it.

  • You understand how legal and communications strategy intersect — and where they can create tension. You know how to navigate that tension thoughtfully.

  • You bring a "no job is too small" attitude. Owning a specialized function doesn't mean you're above the details.

  • You share feedback generously — upward, laterally, and to junior colleagues — and you seek it out with the same energy.

  • You think in systems: you understand how your work connects to team goals, company goals, and business outcomes, and you make that connection visible in how you prioritize and communicate.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6–9 years of communications experience, with significant focus on media relations

  • Demonstrated experience managing sensitive, high-stakes communications in a legal, litigation, regulatory, or crisis context (in-house, agency, or law firm communications)

  • Proven ability to work directly with and influence senior leadership and legal counsel

  • Track record of owning complex cross-functional projects with minimal oversight

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • In-house experience at a publicly traded company

  • Familiarity with securities litigation, class action, or regulatory enforcement communications

  • Experience working alongside outside counsel and understanding the communications boundaries litigation counsel establishes

​Transferable Skills

Here at Zillow - we value the experience and perspective of candidates with non-traditional backgrounds. We encourage you to apply if you have transferable skills or related experiences.

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help customers navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company that's reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.

No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.

About the job

As part of the Technology Distribution team of Tether Data, we are seeking an Engagement Manager to lead the implementation of AI-driven initiatives powered by QVAC, Tether’s SDK for local AI and delegated inference. The role focuses on orchestrating complex, multi-stakeholder deployments of decentralized AI solutions across enterprise, government, and institutional environments.

This position combines client engagement, technical coordination, and delivery oversight to ensure successful onboarding and execution of AI use cases, ranging from edge AI deployments to privacy-preserving inference systems. The Engagement Manager plays a central role in aligning client objectives with product capabilities, coordinating internal and external stakeholders, and driving implementations from initial scoping through production rollout.

Responsibilities

Client & Partner Engagement

  • Act as the primary point of contact for clients and partners during AI implementation initiatives, ensuring clear communication, expectation alignment, and structured execution.

  • Guide clients in translating business requirements into AI deployment strategies leveraging QVAC capabilities (local inference, delegated compute, privacy-preserving architectures).

  • Support Expansion team in shaping AI-related opportunities by providing input on feasibility, integration complexity, and delivery approach.

  • Identify opportunities to extend implementations across additional use cases, geographies, or Tether technologies.

Implementations Oversight

  • Lead end-to-end coordination of QVAC-based implementations from kickoff through production deployment.

  • Define implementation roadmaps, milestones, and dependencies across AI models, infrastructure, and integration layers.

  • Ensure alignment between client expectations and actual product capabilities, avoiding scope drift or mispositioning.

  • Track progress across multiple concurrent AI deployments, ensuring timely delivery and readiness for production environments.

Cross-functional Coordination

  • Coordinate closely with product, engineering, and research teams to align on QVAC capabilities, limitations, and roadmap evolution.

  • Facilitate integration between client systems and QVAC components, including model deployment pipelines, APIs, and compute environments.

  • Work with legal and compliance teams where required, particularly in sensitive AI deployments involving data locality or privacy constraints.

  • Maintain structured communication flows across all stakeholders involved in the implementation lifecycle.

Governance & Reporting

  • Establish and maintain governance frameworks including implementation plans, risk tracking, and decision logs.

  • Produce executive-level updates summarizing progress, risks, blockers, and next steps.

  • Ensure documentation of implementation architectures, deployment patterns, and key learnings for reuse across future projects.

  • Support escalation management and ensure timely resolution of technical or operational challenges.

Requirements

Core Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in program management, technical account management, or delivery roles within AI, data infrastructure, or complex technology environments.

  • Proven experience managing cross-functional implementations involving multiple stakeholders (internal teams, clients, external partners).

  • Strong ability to operate at the intersection of technical and business domains.

Technical Understanding

  • Familiarity with AI/ML deployment concepts, including model inference, edge/local AI, and distributed compute architectures.

  • Understanding of APIs, SDK integrations, and system architecture patterns.

  • Ability to engage in technical discussions with engineering teams while maintaining business-level clarity with clients.

Communication & Execution

jobs.excerpt: This is a remote position. The VisionSignalmash is a CPaaS company: SMS (10DLC, Toll-Free, and Short Code), RCS, SIP trunking, VoIP PBX solutions, and voice infrastructure.
jobs.description:
This is a remote position.

The Vision

Signalmash is a CPaaS company: SMS (10DLC, Toll-Free, and Short Code), RCS, SIP trunking, VoIP PBX solutions, and voice infrastructure. We exist in the same space occupied by Twilio, Telnyx, and Bandwidth. We run an established, revenue-generating wholesale voice business with a stronghold in text messaging services for US businesses. (Preferable) Experience with voice and SMS in omnichannel communications is a strong plus, but drive matters more than background. If you're self-motivated, accountable, and eager to master new technologies alongside a collaborative team, we want to hear from you.

Our customers today come from inbound demand and from our reputation in the voice market. What we have not built yet is the outbound muscle; no validated outbound ICP, no battle-tested messaging, no internal conversion benchmarks. That is not a gap we are hiding, it is the job.

We are actively looking to hire four dedicated & experienced Sales Development Representatives (SDR’s) to build the outbound motion from first principles: figure out which ICP converts, what messaging converts leads into clients, what objections exist in the market and work as a team to determine a path forward on how to beat them, and turn all of it into a documented playbook. If you have only ever executed someone else's playbook, this role might not be for you. If you’ve always wanted to be the person who has a say on what needs to be done to create a successful playbook, you’re in the right place.

Why This Beats a Bigger Logo

  • Ownership, not headcount:At a large company you are an employee number, potentially one templated email away from a layoff. With Signalmash, you have a name, your work is visible to the entire company, and the playbook you build carries your fingerprints.

  • You will work directly with the founding team and C-Suite executives. The people taking the meetings you book are the same people you work side by side with. No layers, no politics, no waiting three levels for a decision.

  • A real leadership path:Whoever builds the playbook and proves a predictable pipeline earns the shot at heading the outbound team, hiring and building it around their own system. We expect to make that call within 6 to 12 months, decided on results, not tenure.

  • Skills that compound:This is where actual selling ability gets tested and built; cold conversations, message crafting, & market discovery – The rep who does this well becomes twice the professional they were. You will learn new skills & tactics as you grow with the company, skills that have overlap into any software-based company.

What You Will Do

  • Own the full outbound motion for your territory/ICP: account selection, contact mapping, multi-channel cadences (calls, email, LinkedIn), and booking qualified meetings for the AE team.

  • Form and test ICP hypotheses against our strongest signal, our existing customer base, and kill or scale them based on data.

  • Build the playbook as you go: messaging that gets responses, an objection taxonomy with working rebuttals, cadence structures, and internal benchmarks.

  • Run a written learning log and a weekly funnel review with the sales team. You get full transparency and support on tap; you drive your own ramp.

Hours and Work-Life Commitments

This is a US-hours role:7:00 PM to 3:00 AM IST, covering East Coast mornings through West Coast afternoons.We are specific about balance instead of vague about culture:

  • No day-shift meetings stacked on top of your night.

  • Saturdays and Sundays fully off. No weekend pipeline reviews, ever.

  • Recover, rejuvenate, and start each week fresh. We believe that burned-out reps build nothing, and it’s important to get the rest you need to excel.


Requirements

Who We Are Looking For

  • 3+ years of outbound B2B SaaS sales experience selling into the US market with average deal size of $2500+/month, with the call recordings and funnel numbers to prove it.

  • Immaculate English, spoken and written, near-native fluency. You will spend your day on the phone with US decision-makers.

  • Evidence of building, not just running: a territory you opened, messaging you wrote, a process you created that others used.

  • Experience of handling mid-market deals with multiple stakeholders.

  • Structured and self-directed. Full transparency and support, but no script handed to you, because none exists yet.

  • Comfortable with technical products, sales AI workflows or demonstrably fast at learning them.

Remote Setup Requirements

  • Dedicated quiet workspace

  • Reliable high-speed internet with a backup connection

About Aalyria:

Aalyria is a leading technology company that supplies laser communications technology and temporospatial software-defined networking platforms to the aerospace industry. With technology acquired from Google, Aalyria is at the forefront of innovation in satellite and airborne mesh networks, as well as cislunar and deep-space communications. We are revolutionizing the orchestration and management of planetary mesh networks using any radio or optical spectrum, any orbit, and any hardware across land, sea, air, and space.

Role Overview:

The Aalyria Tightbeam team focuses on delivering the world’s most advanced optical communication solutions. As an electrical engineer working on the team you will develop and deliver systems for our next-generation land, sea, air & space optical communications terminals and support systems. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems as we continue to push technology forward. With your technical expertise you will manage project priorities, deadlines, and deliverables. You will personally design, develop, test, deploy, maintain, and enhance electrical engineering solutions.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with a cross-functional team on electronics integration, troubleshooting, and optimization for free-space optical (FSO) technology.
  • Assist design and development of all aspects of electronics design from individual PCBAs to higher level system integrations.
  • Use ECAD tools to design custom PCBAs including digital and mixed signal circuitry.
  • Research and select electronics components, and create and maintain CAD libraries to support PCBA design.
  • Assist in documentation of designs, test plans, and technical reports for internal teams and project stakeholders as well as customers.
  • Perform tests on the benchtop, during integration, and for experimental data collection.
  • Create wiring and cable drawings for individual assemblies as well as connection diagrams between individual PCBAs and higher level assemblies.
  • Assist as technical POC for electronics with vendors, customers, and other internal stakeholders.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent practical experience.
  • Up to 3 years of electrical engineering experience in embedded systems for industrial applications.
  • Ability to design PCBAs using ECAD design software (KiCAD, Altium, etc).
  • Experience in all phases of designing circuits boards, including circuit design and component selection, schematic capture, PCB layout, and manufacturing.
  • Familiarity with Electrical Engineering lab fundamentals and electronic test equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, multi-meters, etc.).
  • Passion for being in the lab, problem solving, and engineering.
  • Experience with bringing up and debugging prototype PCBAs.
  • Foundational knowledge in design for manufacture and new product introduction.
  • Experience with wire/cable assembly design or wiring diagrams.
  • Understanding of designing for compliance with industry standards (FCC, UL, etc.)
  • Familiarity with board and system level power analysis.
  • Experience with specifying acceptance tests, design of experiments, data collection, and data analysis.
  • Comfortable traveling and working in a broad range of deployment environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3 - 6 years of electrical engineering experience in designing electronics for industrial,
  • aerospace, or military applications.
  • Experience with KiCAD EDA software.
  • Foundational knowledge of designing and laying out circuits with high speed digital (2.5Gbps+), analog, and mixed signal circuitry.
  • Ability to hand solder and modify circuit boards, perform board level validations, and integrate into larger assemblies.
  • Experience designing, testing, and debugging products compliant with industry EMI/EMC standards (FCC, UL, etc).
  • Experience with wire and cable design for industrial, aerospace, or military applications.
  • Familiarity with version control using Git.
  • Comfortable working with Linux (Ubuntu, embedded Linux) in the terminal.
  • Experience working with embedded C.
  • Familiarity with RF and/or optical link budgets.

During the interview process you are strongly encouraged to present at least one schematic and PCB layout for designs you have personally created. This should be a schematic you have created, and a PCB you have laid out and routed. It can be a work or personal project. You should be able to explain the circuit choices and design tradeoffs made, as well as talk about the PCB layout and routing choices/tradeoffs. Presenting more than one design is not required but not discouraged.

What We Offer:

  • Impactful Work: Directly contribute to critical national security programs and initiatives.

The company reserves the right to decline pursuing an export licensing process for legitimate business-related reasons.

POSITION TITLE:

Strategic Communications

ABOUT OCEAN CONSERVANCY

For more than 50 years, Ocean Conservancy has delivered effective, evidence-based solutions for the ocean and all who depend on it. Today, we continue to unite science, people and policy to protect our ocean from the greatest challenges it faces: climate change, plastic pollution and biodiversity loss. We are a 501(C)3 headquartered in Washington, D.C. that inspires a worldwide network of partners, advocates and supporters through our comprehensive and clear-eyed approach to ocean conservation. Together, we are securing a healthy ocean and a thriving planet, forever and for everyone.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Ghost Gear Communications Strategist will develop and begin implementing a communications strategy to advance Ocean Conservancy’s work on ghost gear (lost, abandoned or discarded fishing gear) which is pound for pound the deadliest form of debris to marine life.

The Strategist will seize opportunities over the next year to advance our conservation work on this critical issue, develop foundational materials and content for ghost gear communications and lay the groundwork to grow Ocean Conservancy’s public footprint on ghost gear over the next five to ten years. The Strategist will also develop a brand guide to ensure alignment between Ocean Conservancy and the Global Ghost Gear Initiative (GGGI), a global alliance convened by Ocean Conservancy that brings together industry, NGOs and governments.

The Strategist will report to the Vice President, Strategic Communications and work in close partnership with both the ghost gear program team and the strategic communications department at Ocean Conservancy.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Develop an understanding of the issue of ghost gear and Ocean Conservancy’s work in this area.
  • Develop foundational materials and content for ghost gear, including:
    • Core messaging on ghost gear
    • Formatted two-pager
    • Video optimized for social media
    • Evergreen social media posts/graphics
    • Carousel explainer on types of ghost gear
    • Video explainers on how ghost gear ends up in our ocean (where it travels, how it impacts animals, etc.)
    • Videos on specific locations
    • Media list / core spokespeople / media pitch
  • Develop communications/branding strategy for ghost gear, which should include:
    • Goals, key audiences, tactics
    • Plan for how we’ll use GGGI social media channels
    • Intersection with Protect Where We Play, our initiative to mobilize the sports and entertainment industry to protect our ocean
    • Opportunities we’ll capitalize on in the next two years, including the Our Ocean conference and report launches
    • Five- and ten-year ghost gear opportunities and communications framing
  • Develop brand guide for Ocean Conservancy/GGGI to ensure alignment in all comms
  • Three public communications moments executed (e.g. launch of new research)

SKILLS/QUALIFICATIONS/EXPERIENCE

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in digital or communications strategy, with a proven track record of developing and launching new communications campaigns and initiatives.
  • Proven ability to produce compelling content across formats: social, long-form, video scripts, email and campaign copy.
  • Strong writing and editing skills with the ability to adapt voice and tone across audiences and channels.
  • Proven track record of securing media coverage.
  • Nonprofit experience a plus.
  • Ability to travel occasionally.

EDUCATION/TRAINING

Bachelor’s degree in Communications or related field preferred.

COMPENSATION

Ocean Conservancy is committed to fair pay practices and posts expected salary ranges for each of its positions. Compensation will be commensurate with the candidate’s specialty skills, years of experience, location, and unique background. The expected pay range for this role is $90 to $100 hourly. We would welcome the opportunity to connect with potential candidates whose salary requirements may be outside of the expected range.

TO APPLY

If you think you’d be a great fit for the job and are interested in joining Ocean Conservancy’s team, please apply here. Please include a resume and cover letter in one file on your application.

HYBRID WORK ENVIRONMENT

Ocean Conservancy embraces a hybrid work environment, which allows our staff the flexibility to work virtually and in-person while building strong connections across the institution.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship for less-experienced members of the team to deliver key ML-powered features for our Digital Customer Platform.

  • Partner with stakeholders, to solve important business objectives across a range of problems

En tant que développeur principal en apprentissage automatique au sein de l’équipe, vous serez chargé de diriger ou de contribuer à la conception, à l’analyse et à la mise en œuvre de solutions fondées sur les données afin de relever des défis d’affaires majeurs dans le cadre de programmes de travail RAG dédiés. Ce poste est axé sur la pratique et met l’accent sur la résolution de problèmes techniques à l’aide des dernières technologies en traitement du langage naturel (TLN) et en apprentissage automatique.

La culture de notre équipe repose sur la collaboration, le soutien mutuel et l’apprentissage continu. En tant que spécialiste principal en apprentissage automatique, vous fournirez des conseils techniques et votre expertise à l’équipe ainsi qu’aux autres parties prenantes. Nous mettons l’accent sur une approche agile, pratique et technique à tous les niveaux de l’équipe.

En tant que groupe, nous souhaitons améliorer continuellement notre apprentissage automatique ainsi que notre connaissance des tendances et des techniques pertinentes pour nos domaines. Notre équipe vise l’excellence tant dans la théorie que dans la pratique de l’apprentissage automatique. Nous encourageons le développement personnel et le partage des connaissances.

Responsabilités

  • Concevoir et mettre en œuvre des capacités d’apprentissage automatique qui améliorent les plateformes RAG d’Autodesk

Qualifications Minimales

  • Maîtrise (MS/M.Tech/M.Math) ou doctorat (Ph.D.) en informatique, statistiques, mathématiques, physique, développement logiciel, économie, linguistique computationnelle ou dans des domaines connexes

Vorstandsmitglied Finanzen und Reporting

Der Street Child Deutschland e.V. sucht eine engagierte Person mit Teamgeist als Mitglied des geschäftsführenden Vorstands mit Fokus auf Finanzen und Reporting. Street Child Deutschland ist Mitglied des seit 20 Jahren bestehenden, internationalen Street Child Netzwerkes. Neben einer engen Zusammenarbeit mit den deutschen Vorstands- und Teamkollegen bietet dieses Ehrenamt auch die Möglichkeiten, unser europäisches Fundraising-Team in Barcelona und London zu unterstützen und mit den Vorstandsmitgliedern im globalen Street Child Netzwerk zusammenzuarbeiten.

jobs.excerpt: REBORRN is a new breed of management consultancy, future-proofing global marketing teams for the age of change.
jobs.description:
REBORRN is a new breed of management consultancy, future-proofing global marketing teams for the age of change. Its proprietary “58” methodology tackles complex business challenges in under three days by bringing the right people together in a focused, agile, and distraction-free environment. REBORRN is a cross-functional team of 55+ experts working across geographies to drive radical transformation through design thinking and hands-on problem-solving.

Focused on fast, impact-driven solutions, REBORRN’s expertise spans every need of a modern marketing team, from Strategy & Transformation to Capability Upskilling, Team Optimisation, CX Transformation, and Experience & Innovation. Over the years, REBORRN has partnered with some of the world’s most influential brands, including The Coca-Cola Company, Philip Morris International, L’Oréal, Nestlé, Bayer, PUIG, and more.

Our team is growing quickly, and we are always looking to enrich our pool with top-tier talent for future opportunities.

Sounds fancy? It’s not. Being part of our team may not be your typical job. We are looking for makers, people who can actually get things done and see them through. And that can be messy.

Happy with that? Read on.

What’s your day-to-day

Our team is diverse in background, superpowers and perspectives. Expect to work daily alongside data scientists, product designers, marketing experts, management consultants and organisational designers. Most of your projects will require you to be part of, or lead, teams of people you have never worked with before.

We work with some of the most influential organisations in the world, including The Coca-Cola Company, L'Oreal, Bayer and Philip Morris International, on a variety of projects. While we are a newborrn consultancy with a very diverse portfolio of engagements, there is a clear pattern in how we approach problem-solving that will give you a sense of what your work at REBORRN would look like.

You will work in agile teams with coworkers and the client to make things happen, whether that means delivering a tough-to-implement action plan, launching a new product to market, or designing and deploying a new process that removes bottlenecks and increases efficiency.

Your job is done when you make yourself obsolete, and you are confident enough to fire yourself from the project.

What kind of projects? Anything from sharpening strategy and turning it into progress by rewiring how teams work and building the capabilities that matter most, to upgrading operating systems and designing consumer experiences that drive growth. It could mean landing a new product line, creating a global campaign process, or rethinking a client’s entire innovation model.

In any of the above cases, you’ll be working in a vibrant environment that’s at times intense with shifting priorities and plenty of challenges. It’s fast-paced, ever-evolving, and definitely not your comfort zone. But one thing is certain: you’ll never get bored.

Requirements

Who you are.

We do not care about your MBA, your corporate background, or your university alumni network. We are far more interested in who you are and what you can bring to the team.

You have experience working in a business role, whether in an established company, a start-up, or a consulting firm. A combination of these would certainly get our attention.

You are an excellent problem solver. You confront challenges with a results-oriented approach and a healthy mix of strategic and creative thinking.

You have a strong record of proactivity and great self-management skills. You see yourself as a highly organised multitasker who can prioritise and meet tight deadlines like a pro, all while keeping a sharp eye for detail.

You are a fast learner with a “can-do-anything” attitude. Seeking feedback comes as naturally as breathing, and you see mistakes as excellent learning opportunities. You are also great with people.

You are tech-savvy and constantly exploring how technology and new tools can make your life easier. You are curious by nature! We are flexible on remote working, so knowing how to operate independently and stay self-organised is important too.

Last but not least, you care. At REBORRN, we don’t accept the “this is not my job” mentality. If someone spills coffee on the floor, you pick up the mop and clean it.

Sounds interesting? Take a look at our benefits package below.

Benefits

Our most important perk is offering you an energy-laden workplace with some of the market’s top talent and an opportunity to thrive. Beyond that, here are some highlights:

  • Top-notch tech gear
  • Unlimited vacation policy
  • Private medical insurance
  • Flexible on remote working
  • Fast growth opportunities
  • Competitive Income Standards
  • All-you-can-read books policy
  • Public transport travel card
  • Subscription for an e-Scooter or a bike
  • Stock Options Scheme
  • Amazing office space in the heart of Athens

jobs.description:
Fairmont is seeking an experienced, strategic, and highly motivated Senior Area Sales Manager to support the commercial efforts of three luxury resorts within the Mexico & Caribbean region: Fairmont Mayakoba, Fairmont El San Juan Hotel, and Fairmont Royal Pavilion.

This role will be based remotely in the United States, with Fairmont Mayakoba serving as the home property, while maintaining clear responsibility for generating business across all three hotels. The Senior Area Sales Manager will focus on new business development, account management, prospecting, and revenue generation across key market segments, with a strong emphasis on group, incentive, corporate, and third-party business.

This is a highly strategic sales role requiring a strong background in luxury hospitality, proactive selling, relationship-driven account management, and regional collaboration. The ideal candidate will be comfortable representing multiple properties, balancing competing priorities, and partnering closely with regional and on-property leadership to drive revenue, expand market share, and identify opportunities across the portfolio.

What Is in It for You

  • Opportunity to represent three iconic Fairmont resorts across Mexico & the Caribbean
  • Ability to work remotely while being part of a highly collaborative regional commercial team
  • Opportunity to develop your talent and grow within Accor and Fairmont
  • Exposure to a regional commercial platform with cross-functional leadership opportunities
  • Ability to make a meaningful impact across multiple luxury properties

Key Responsibilities

Business Development & Revenue Generation

  • Represent Fairmont Mayakoba, Fairmont El San Juan Hotel, and Fairmont Royal Pavilion in the marketplace and actively solicit new business opportunities across assigned market segments.
  • Drive revenue production through proactive prospecting, account development, client engagement, and strategic relationship management across all three hotels.
  • Maintain, grow, and strategically develop key accounts while aggressively pursuing new business opportunities that align with each hotel’s revenue goals and need periods.
  • Build and execute monthly action plans designed to drive room night production, revenue growth, and market share across the region.
  • Exceed individual production goals and activity targets as established by the Regional Director of Sales & Marketing.

Regional Commercial Collaboration

  • Partner closely with the Regional Director of Sales & Marketing, hotel DOSMs, revenue leaders, and marketing teams to ensure alignment on sales strategy, need periods, and business priorities.
  • Support each hotel’s revenue goals through disciplined prospecting, account management, and conversion efforts.
  • Participate in regular regional pipeline, forecast, and strategy discussions.
  • Identify new business opportunities that support the broader commercial platform across the Mexico & Caribbean region.
  • Serve as a regional ambassador for the three properties, ensuring consistent representation of each hotel in the marketplace.

Administrative & Operational Responsibilities

  • Ensure all business opportunities are qualified appropriately and managed in accordance with hotel policies and commercial strategy.
  • Maintain a high level of professionalism, responsiveness, and luxury service standards in all client and internal interactions.

Work independently with strong initiative while managing multiple priorities across

  • Minimum 5+ years of hotel sales experience, preferably within luxury hospitality
  • Proven experience driving new business development, prospecting, and account management
  • Experience selling group, incentive, corporate, or third-party business
  • Prior experience representing multiple hotels, regions, or brands is strongly preferred
  • Strong understanding of luxury hospitality sales and the ability to position multiple resorts within a competitive marketplace
  • Excellent communication, presentation, and relationship-building abilities
  • Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail
  • Experience with Opera, Delphi / Salesforce / CRM systems, and Microsoft Office preferred
  • Experience negotiating and executing contracts and related agreements
  • Bachelor’s degree or Hotel Management degree/diploma preferred

Travel Requirements

  • This role is remote and based in the United States; however, regular travel will be required in support of Fairmont Mayakoba, Fairmont El San Juan Hotel, and Fairmont Royal Pavilion.
  • Travel may include client visits, site inspections, trade shows, sales missions, FAM trips, and on-property meetings.

Candidate must be able to travel domestically and internationally as business needs

Physical Aspects of Position

Physical aspects of the position include but are not limited to:

  • Frequent sitting throughout shift
  • Occasional lifting and carrying up to 20 lbs
  • Occasional kneeling, pushing, pulling, and lifting
  • Frequent travel, including air travel and overnight stays, may be required

Employee Benefits:

Join our team and enjoy a range of exclusive colleague perks, including complimentary upgrades, extended stays, discounted stays across Fairmont & Raffles properties, special dining and wellness discounts, and added luxuries to enhance your experience. We believe in taking care of our team, ensuring that your hard work is rewarded with exceptional benefits.

Our Values

Respect:

We value the needs, ideas and individuality of others. We treat everyone with fairness and dignity. 

Excellence:

We make genuine connections, and we cherish every opportunity to make the people around us feel special.​

Belonging:

We celebrate our differences. We support each other and we always stand together.​

We have authority to take initiative and anticipate moments that create unforgettable experiences. ​

Integrity:

We build trust through mutual respect and being authentic.​

Diversity & Inclusion

Fairmont is committed to creating an inclusive environment where diverse talent thrives. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to join our team.

Working within the Global Clinical Affairs (GCA) organization, the Senior Clinical Project Manager is responsible for clinical trial management of multiple studies and may be subject matter expert for group or platform of assigned clinical studies including the planning, implementation, oversight, project management and completion of clinical trials conducted by GCA or Contract Research Organizations (CRO).   • Ensures execution within overall study timelines and deliverables and delivers accordingly for his/her studies.
  • Proactively identifies, escalates and manages risks and issues to ensure cost-effective timely delivery of the project
  • Collaborates actively with other GCA functions, e.g. global project management, as applicable, DM and Statistics
  • Collaborates with the Medical Affairs departments of the BD Business Units
  • Oversees/leads and trains study-specific local clinical resources, e.g. contractor CRA, CRO, etc.
  • Provides critical thinking and escalates accordingly when issues arise during execution of clinical studies.
  • Oversees study quality and implements high quality standards in order to meet compliance requirements
  • Contributes to continuous improvement activities/initiatives,
  • Manages relationships with sites/PIs and other study-related vendors, e.g. CROs, central labs, etc.

About You

  • Bachelor's degree required, preferably in the life sciences, clinical or other relevant technical areas
  • Minimum of 4 years project management experience
  • Minimum 6 years of clinical study experience, (e.g., preferably in medical device, or in IVD, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, CRO) including the proven ability to oversee clinical teams in the conduct and report of multicenter, global complex studies
  • Familiarity with CLSI guidelines and other standards
  • Demonstrable Project Management skills; PMP Certification is a preferred goal for all Clinical Project Managers;
  • Proficient understanding of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), FDA and ISO regulations, MDR/IVDR and current industry practices related to the conduct of clinical studies
  • Knowledge of clinical trial concepts and practices, including international clinical research guidelines and regulations
  • Strong client and vendor relationship management skills
  • Ability to work effectively, mostly independently in international teams, manage multiple projects and work in a fast paced and changing environment
  • Demonstrated and effective interpersonal, communications and negotiation skills for a wide variety of audiences
  • Ability to work effectively in a virtual environment
  • Ability to travel approximately 20%, worldwide

Our Offer

A professional challenge in a highly motivated team, a global environment and with long-term perspectives. A familiar working atmosphere in an innovative environment where your opinion matters. Diversity characterizes our corporate culture and we are convinced that it makes us a stronger team. We value each person as an individual with their abilities and needs. In this sense, we welcome applicants who wish to work part-time, people with severe disabilities and applicants of any gender.

jobs.description:
Responsibilities

100% Remote Emergency Radiologist (FL, MO, WA, CT, MA, NH, VT, ME)

Evening and Overnight Shifts, Full and Part Time options, Huge salary upside

Dartmouth Health’s Department of Radiology is seeking fully Remote Evening and Overnight Emergency Teleradiologists (FL, MO, WA, CT, MA, NH, VT, ME). This is a high-paying job with plenty of time off to travel and live life, offering a vibrant and fulfilling career, and being part of a thriving department. Fully remote Evening and Overnight Emergency Radiologists have no on-site responsibilities, though they are valued members of our department helping us cover multiple Dartmouth Health facilities located throughout New Hampshire and Vermont. Dartmouth Radiology is a leading, nationally known radiology enterprise covering all modalities and all radiology subspecialties.

Position Summary

Dartmouth Health is seeking a remote evening and nighttime radiologist to join our Emergency Radiology imaging division. Evening and overnight work consists of a standard emergency radiology case mix, comprised mostly of straight -forward x-rays, CTs, and Ultrasounds. We have limited overnight and evening MRs acquired as well. Our evening and overnight coverage is a team model, so candidates with specific strengths or weakness can often be accommodated.

We cover the Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center, which is a level I Trauma Center and has a Comprehensive Stroke Center, as well as imaging from other surrounding facilities. The Emergency radiology schedule is a 7-day-on, 14-days-off schedule with staggered, overlapping shifts covering the evening and overnight hours.

The Department values patient-centered care and a highly collaborative, respectful, caring, and engaging work environment. There is a strong working relationship with other Departments.

We are able to employ radiologists from Florida, Missouri, Washington state, Connecticut, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Vermont, and Maine.

Though Dartmouth radiology is home to outstanding training programs, remote radiologists do not have direct educational responsibilities. We do welcome candidates who are interested in occasionally lecturing or other engagements with our educational mission, though participation in entirely voluntary without any core expectations built into the role. Remote radiologists do not routinely read out radiology residents, though limited resident interaction is possible. Our remote radiology team is also not expected to participate in research or other scholarly activities, though again, we welcome candidates who may have targeted interested and we aim to be supportive of candidate’s professional goals.

All remote radiologists will be full members of the Department as well as valued W-2 employees of Dartmouth Health. Remote readers are provided a Dartmouth owned reading station with a full suite of our standard PACS software.

Compensation

Remote radiologists are W-2 benefited employees who are compensated via our productivity-based Radiology Compensation plan. The plan offers a competitive guaranteed starting salary with opportunity for productivity incentives in addition to base.

All remote radiologists receive employer-provided retirement contributions, including a generous matching program, which are in addition to one’s salary. Medical malpractice is provided. There is a generous health insurance option specifically for remote employees.

Our faculty are encouraged to participate in continuing education, national societies, and professional development organizations, depending on the faculty’s interest and needs. We support these efforts with institutional funds allocated to each faculty member.

Schedule

The Emergency radiology schedule is a 7-day-on, 14-days-off schedule with staggered, overlapping shifts covering the evening and overnight hours. We have opportunities to do additional hours or add-on shifts (analogous to internal moonlighting) for those seeking additional income. A full-time position involves completing 4 weeks of work every 12 weeks (one week out of every three), and we have options for individuals to do part time roles (including completing 3 or 2 weeks of work every 12 weeks).

Clinical Excellence

The Department prides itself on high-quality, efficient, modern imaging and very much prizes our clinical service and the care provided to our patients. Remote readers will have an essential role in contributing to our core clinical mission. We value the engagement of all radiologists on our team, including remote radiologist, in our robust peer learning program and all quality systems. We value input on the imaging provided and clinical services rendered.

The Department values patient-centered care and a highly collaborative, respectful, caring, and engaging work environment. We value remote radiologists’ contributions to our positive and caring culture. There is a strong working relationship with other Departments, and all referrers.

Benefits:

  • Market leading, highly competitive salaries.
  • Remote readers are eligible for our generous retirement programs with institutional-contributions and a matching program.
  • Remote radiologist roles are fully benefited positions that include malpractice insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, as well as an affordable medical plan.
  • CME funds
  • Incredible department culture which is respectful, transparent, communicative, supportive, optimistic, constructive, and engaged; this culture permeates the department including our on-site and remote workforce. We value our sense of community and our connection to each other.

To learn more, please visit:

www.DHproviders.org

Cover Letters should be addressed to:

David M. Naeger, MD FACR FAAR

Chair, Department of Radiology

CV and cover letter to be sent to:

Caitlin Vecchio, MBA, CPRP-DEI

The Department and Dartmouth Health

The selected candidates will join Dartmouth Health’s 70 radiologists. We are an internationally-known Department with a deep history in the field, beginning with acquiring the first clinical x-ray in the United States in 1896. Since then, we have continued an upward trajectory growing in breadth and depth and expanding our services across New England.

While Dartmouth Health includes many hospitals and clinic sites, our central hub is the tertiary-care Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center, which is the system’s one and only Academic Medical Center. DHMC is the state’s only Level 1 trauma center, a certified Comprehensive Stroke Center, and home to an NCI-designated Comprehensive Cancer Center. Dartmouth runs a fleet of helicopter and ground-based medical transport services connecting facilities and patients throughout New England.

Dartmouth Health maintains a total of 802 beds, with 458 located at DHMC. Our extensive network handles over 3 million outpatient visits annually, supported by a dedicated team of 15,000 employees and more than 2,300 employed providers. Our commitment to the community is reflected in our contributions, with over $345 million in community benefits and $16 million in charity care. These numbers underscore our role as a leading healthcare provider, committed to both clinical excellence and community support.

Required Licensure/Certifications

  • Diagnostic Radiology Board Certified or Board Eligible
  • Must obtain and maintain a medical license in New Hampshire, Vermont, and the candidate’s state of residence.
  • Currently, we are able to employ remote readers who live in, and will read from, FL, MO, WA, CT, MA, NH, VT, and/or ME. We require a fixed address (or addresses), from which readers will provide services. More than 1 address is acceptable as long as all addresses are within the 7 states listed above and the radiologist’s current location is provided at all times.

This is a 1099 independent contractor role and is not an employment (W-2) position. As an independent contractor, you will not be eligible for employee benefits, including but not limited to health insurance, paid time off, workers’ compensation, or unemployment benefits. Pomelo Care will provide services to support your independent practice, such as client matching, billing and administrative support.

Credentialing process & next steps:

As the Vice President of Commercial Strategies and Initiatives, you will play a pivotal leadership role in shaping the future of value-based care. Reporting directly to the Chief Commercial Officer, you will serve as a key architect behind our long-term commercial innovation, designing scalable venture strategies and building new, non-MSSP revenue streams.
